title: Singularity-aware Optimization via Randomized Geometric Probing: Towards Stable Non-smooth Optimization
claim: Standard adaptive optimizers oscillate chaotically near non-smooth minima, while instability-aware damping yields a stable, direct convergence path.
layout: 2x2 grid; contour trajectory plots plus a dual-axis curve; trajectories overlaid cumulatively
description: A 2x2 grid of plots on a synthetic 2-D non-smooth landscape, drawn as grayscale contours. Panel (a) shows a green dashed straight line from a black X start point at (-1.5, -0.5) to a green star global minimum at (1, 1), the ideal trajectory. Panel (b) adds AdamW (red) and Prox-SGD (orange) paths. Both head toward the minimum, then swirl and zigzag chaotically around it. Panel (c) is a dual-axis line plot over steps. A blue S-Adam distance-to-optimum curve falls smoothly, while a green dashed LGI variance signal spikes violently. Panel (d) overlays the smooth blue S-Adam path on the baseline paths, reaching the minimum directly. The eye goes first to the tangled red and orange scribbles in (b), then to the clean blue line in (d). Captions (a)–(d) sit under each panel.
caption: Geometric instability visualization on synthetic non-smooth landscape of $f(x,y) = |x-1| + |y-1| + 0.5(x^2 + y^2)$
abstract: Deep learning optimization relies heavily on the assumption of smooth loss landscapes, a condition systematically violated by modern architectures due to non-smooth components such as ReLU activations and quantization operators. In such non-smooth regimes, adaptive optimizers such as Adam suffer from gradient chattering, violent oscillations caused by conflicting signals within the Clarke subdifferential, leading to poor convergence and suboptimal generalization. To address this, we introduce Singularity-aware Adam (S-Adam), a novel optimizer that stabilizes training by dynamically modulating step sizes based on local geometric instability. Our key contribution is the Local Geometric Instability (LGI) metric, a computationally efficient estimator of the Clarke subdifferential diameter derived from the variance of randomized directional derivatives. S-Adam incorporates an adaptive damping mechanism exp(-$Î»$$Ï$) that decelerates updates in high-instability regions while preserving fast convergence in smooth basins. We provide a rigorous convergence analysis using differential inclusions, proving that S-Adam converges almost surely to ($Î´$,$Îµ$)-Clarke stationary points at the optimal O(1/$\sqrt(T)$) rate. Empirical evaluations on Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) and high-noise small-batch learning demonstrate that S-Adam consistently outperforms AdamW and Prox-SGD, achieving accuracy gains of up to +4.54% on CIFAR-100 and +4.27% on TinyImageNet while effectively mitigating gradient oscillations.
